text: Semantic change across multiple time periods
GroupXXXXX   Milestone   1
Task 3   Subtask 1
Discover sense groups from dated word usages, then track their distribution across periods.
Cluster IDs are arbitrary. These English examples are illustrative.
Team review draft   23 November 2026

35 seconds. The project studies word senses over time. Our scope is Subtask 1. A system groups usages by meaning and uses those groups across time. The example is illustrative and not from the Swedish data. We have prepared the data and method plan; no neural model result is claimed. Source: https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17510/. Course scope: supplied course project description, page 1. This deck is a team-review draft; member names and final ownership remain pending.

40 seconds. We downloaded the official development archive. It contains only Swedish at this stage. We have 1,983 usages for ten words. The package includes references. The text field is named text, and start/end mark the target. We use period_label for evaluation; definitions.jsonl belongs to Subtask 2. Data source: https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17510/. Download URL and SHA-256: 04_data/raw/download_manifest.json. Counts: 04_data/processed/eda_summary.json. All periods are not present for every word, which is shown next.

Counts vary from 98 to 291. Five exact-text pairs have distinct official IDs.

50 seconds. These are measured counts from the data, not model results. Coverage differs across words. Half the words have only five periods. There is a long gap between the historical and modern periods; no observations fill it. 262 usages, or 13.21 percent, have multiple reference labels. A first single-label method cannot express all memberships. All keys align and the spans are nonempty and in bounds. We preserve five repeated-text pairs because official IDs differ. Sources: 04_data/processed/eda_summary.json; quality_audit.json. Reproduce with 03_analysis/milestone_analysis.py.

text:
35 seconds. We selected three publications from explicitly allowed venues. The first motivates clustering contextual usages. The second provides a multilingual target-aware representation candidate. The third supports controlled comparison and separate evaluation of sense induction. We are adapting a method plan; no claim of reproducing their results is made. Citations: https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.365/
https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-short.135/
https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.240/. Full bibliographic details appear on backup slide 7 and in 05_literature/references.bib.
Proposed method and evaluation
GroupXXXXX   Milestone   5
1   Preserve target spans and encode usages with XL-LEXEME
2   Cluster all periods jointly for each target word
3   Compare clustering choices and export integer label lists
Five development folds hold out two complete words each. Seed 445.
Neural experiments remain planned. The scorer integration check is complete.

65 seconds. The first candidate encodes marked target usages using the pretrained XL-LEXEME model. We cluster jointly across periods so label identity is stable. Start with K-means, selecting K from 2 to 10 by silhouette, then compare the single-cluster control and affinity propagation. K>=2 can force splits, so we must examine that limitation. We propose five word-level development folds with seed 445. Gold labels are for tuning on other words and evaluation, not inputs to clustering. EDA used all released words, so this is development validation. Official scorer commit 0e69238bf8b69b4ea0933627ed14e6ca2769d670 computes base-2 Jensen-Shannon distance and filters pairs below ten usages. It retains 60 of 65 candidate transitions. Single-cluster diagnostic BCubed F1 is 0.7563; it is not neural performance. Constant change scores have undefined correlation; the scorer returns zero. Sources: https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.365/; https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-short.135/; https://github.com/ChangeIsKey/semeval2027-task3. Full diagnostic: 04_data/processed/scorer_diagnostic.json.
